questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always wanted to live in Paris, because I love the city. I also wanted to improve my French.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not always easy, because some information wasn't available online beforehand or at least difficult to find.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I received information by e-mail from my host university. There was also an introduction week, where some questions were clarified. 
However, the administration would often not reply to e-mails, if you asked them questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I applied for Fondation Danoise at Cité Universitaire. I would highly recommend this student residence.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend applying for Cité Universitaire, since it's inexpensive compared to other places in Paris and only 15-20 minutes away from the university and the city center by public transport. However, you are not guaranteed a spot (you get a reply in the beginning of July), so it's good to have a plan B.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You chose your courses online about a week before the semester starts. A long time went by without knowing how to apply. 
The schedule for the different courses could undergo changes even after the semester had started. Therefore, all exchange students initially had to choose courses worth of more than 30 ECTS points in case some of the lectures would undergo time changes and overlap. 
We then later had to go to the office at the university and have the incoming coordinator remove the extra courses manually (so we only had 30 points). This was a little complicated and time consuming, since the waiting lines in front of the office were very long.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could e-mail the incoming coordinator, but they wouldn't always answer. You could also show up at their office during opening hours.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have patience and know that the schedule can undergo changes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was appropriate. I only had lectures, so no assigned reading. Even though the classes were only 4 or 6 ECTS points, you learned a lot and the teachers went in depth with the subject. This meant that sometimes the courses would feel like they were worth more than 4 or 6 ECTS points.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I only chose CM courses which meant that there were no books, but only lectures (a lot of the times without powerpoint). During the lectures, you had to write down everything the professors said, since this was the curriculum and the only information available. This was very different from what I'm used to at UCPH. However, it did give me a lot of free time during the semester, since there was no assigned reading or assignments, which was nice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Droit de l'Union Européenne, Droit international public, Philosophie du droit, Legal Cultures, Philosophy of Law and Crossborder Litigation.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the courses in English, if your French Level is below B2. Crossborder Litigation was very interesting. If you have a French level of B2 or above, I would recommend the French courses, but without travaux dirigés.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were more expensive than what I excepted. However, at Cité Universitaire, you can get a warm meal for around 3 euros which was very nice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't look into any of them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Student associations and trips to for exemple the Senate or l'Assemblée Nationale.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't attend any so I don't know. I mainly socialized with other students during breaks between lectures and at Cité Universitaire, where I lived. There were a lot of social activities and opportunities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore Paris and visit the different neighborhoods. There are so many things to do in the city and museums are also free for EU-citizens under 26 years old. For trips outside of Paris, I recommend Versailles and other French cities, that you can reach by train, such as Bordeaux.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. It's not too different from Denmark, but there are of course some difference. I would say that speaking French is an advantage, but it's not crucial.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The French students are very nice, helpful and welcoming.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
The French school system is very different from the Danish one. For the exams, you have to learn everything by heart, since no documents are allowed. This was something I wasn't used to, since we can usually bring books and notes to the exams at UCPH.
Administrative procedures in France are very slow and long.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, the people and the art. Paris has amazing culture in general.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Speaking French is an advantage, but not crucial, have patience with the administration, but be persistent and don't be afraid to ask the French students for help.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Apply for Cité Universitaire (inexpensive, great social life and a very nice place to live as a student). 
CM courses (cours magistraux) are a lot less demanding than courses with travaux dirigés. I would therefore recommend cours magistraux.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to experience living in Paris and improving my French a lot.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The administration and the exam period, since I had 6 exams in 2 weeks where I had to learn everything by heart and 3 of the exams were in French.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
